did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with a heading identifying it as a “Psalm of David” and designating it “for the director of music, according to the Gittith.” The verse itself does not explain what the Gittith is, so it can only be said that it is related to the performance instructions for the psalm.

Did you know? From the very beginning, the psalm declares the greatness of the Lord throughout the earth: his name is majestic, and his glory is described as being set above the heavens. In this way, the verse connects the earthly world with the heavenly realm.

Did you know? The psalm presents the mouths of infants and nursing babies as the source of a foundation of strength; according to the rest of the verse, this strength is connected with silencing the enemy and the avenger.

Did you know? The psalmist’s reflection on creation includes the heavens, the moon, and the stars. The stars are described as the work of the Lord’s fingers—a poetic expression emphasizing the power of creation and how effortlessly its Creator brought it about.

Did you know? In view of the vastness of the heavens, the psalmist asks two parallel questions: “What is mankind that you remember them?” and “What is a human being that you care for them?” These questions express wonder that human beings receive divine attention.

Did you know? The verse describes humanity’s status in two ways: on the one hand, people are made a little lower, while on the other, they are crowned with glory and honor. In this way, humility and greatness are emphasized together.

Did you know? According to the psalm, humanity has been given authority over the works of the Lord’s hands, and everything that was created has been placed under its feet. This description presents human beings as having authority and responsibility within the created world.
Did you know? The list of creatures placed under human authority includes sheep and cattle—that is, domesticated animals—as well as the beasts of the field.

Did you know? The dominion described in the psalm is not limited to the land. It also includes the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, as well as everything that travels along the paths of the seas.

Did you know? The psalm ends by repeating almost exactly its opening declaration: “Lord, our Lord, how majestic is your name throughout the earth!” This repetition creates a framework and emphasizes that humanity and all creation stand beneath the greatness of the Lord.
